reason: The cold case needs a supporting shell, so combining the metal stock with the refrigeration insert seems like a useful start.
expectation: I expect to make a case or frame fitted with refrigeration, though it may still need insulation and cold packs.

alternatives.reason: Freezing the cold packs also seems necessary, but I want to build the case first.

effect: The metal and insert formed a powered field case with a core cradle and an external radiator; it still appears to need insulation.
reaction: The radiator detail is interesting because it explains how the case can shed heat in the thin Martian atmosphere.
reason: Adding insulation seems like the natural next step to help the case keep the core cold.
expectation: I expect an insulated refrigerated case, though the cold packs may still need to be prepared separately.

alternatives.reason: Freezing the packs also seems useful for the trip, but I want to finish the case first.

effect: The case is insulated while its radiator and power connection remain accessible; the cold packs are the remaining preparation.
reaction: Keeping the radiator exposed makes practical sense.
reason: Freezing the cold packs is the only available combination and should prepare them for the trip.
expectation: I expect the freezer to chill the packs for use with the field case.

effect: The cold packs are ready to absorb heat during a limited transfer, with spare cartridges remaining in the freezer.
reaction: The distinction between temporary heat absorption and active refrigeration is useful.
reason: The only available combination should add the conditioned packs to the insulated case.
expectation: I expect a completed cold case with backup cooling for transfers, though it may still need to be fitted to the rover.

effect: The finished case combines active refrigeration near minus 45 degrees with a short buffer during power changes, completing the goal.
reaction: The packs sliding into pockets around the cradle was satisfying, and their limited role is clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the refrigerated case was most worthwhile because the external radiator explained how it can reject heat in the Martian environment.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the insulation felt was straightforward and reinforced the radiator detail already introduced, so it was the least engaging passage.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the case uses an external Mars-rated radiator and that the cold packs only provide a short margin when power changes.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; each contributed to the case, although the last two combinations were the only available gameplay choices.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to collect the second core and learn what the receiving lab finds, and the cooling details made this preparation interesting.
